methodology: Only public universities are in scope: private institutions are excluded before any other gate, so no ownership tag is carried on a row. Universities are retained only when all inclusive gates are evidenced: EduRank 2026 overall world rank of 1,000 or better nationwide, or 3,200 or better for a qualifying programme campus in a city already listed in the German city scoreboard; at least one current on-campus, computing-centred degree that accepts foreign credentials and can be completed in English; and mandatory Bangladeshi/non-EU tuition of €5,000 or less per semester. English admission evidence or isolated English modules do not establish an English-completable pathway. Domain programmes qualify only when computing is central and a CSE-related prior degree is explicitly accepted. Intake tags describe programme entry seasons, not admission eligibility. Open now is reserved for a current explicitly dated official cycle. Annual window open means today falls within a standing recurring rule; Annual dates has no confirmed current cycle. Closed for summer records the relevant passed summer window. Window unverified means the current window was not established, including rows outside this focused review. Future Opens tags require an explicitly published relevant-cycle opening. Exactly one admission-status tag and one applicant-funding tag are used. Tuition-free does not cover living costs; Funding needed marks paid programmes under Tanima’s full-funding requirement; Funding unverified records unresolved programme tuition. The university inclusion ceiling remains EUR 5,000 per semester, while the applicant’s funding filter is stricter. Rankings, row order and campus pins are retained, not freshly re-ranked. Evidence review scope is stated on each row; official university sources govern programme rules and DAAD provides cross-checks.
caveats: The shortlist is public-universities-only by design. Private institutions are out of scope and are never listed, whatever their rank or English provision.
The inclusion rules are conjunctive: failing rank, English-completable computing programme, international admission, or tuition removes the institution.
Admission is not guaranteed. Every applicant must match formal subject-credit, grade and language rules; software work experience rarely replaces missing academic credits.
€0 denotes no programme tuition, not free study: semester contributions, application fees, visa funding, insurance and living costs still apply.
Future application dates are stated only when officially published or as clearly labelled recurring programme deadlines; always verify the live portal.
EduRank is an independent bibliometric provider. Overall rank is mandatory; missing subject ranks are not inferred.
Approximate map pins identify the official campus neighbourhood and are not building-entrance coordinates.

City and university datasets remain independent: six listed cities currently have no qualifying local institution after research—Brandenburg an der Havel, Frankfurt (Oder), Oranienburg, Falkensee, Bernau bei Berlin and Eberswalde.

TUM qualifies through M.Sc. Information Engineering at its Heilbronn campus: DAAD lists no tuition and TUM's fee structure implies none, but TUM states no amount for it; its former qualifying programme, Informatics: Games Engineering, now costs €6,000 per semester.
FAU Erlangen charges non-EU students €4,000 per semester from summer 2027 enrolment; this stays within the €5,000 ceiling.
Several programmes require a GRE, GATE or dMat result from Bangladeshi applicants (for example FAU AI, Kassel, Paderborn, FH Aachen and TUM Heilbronn); read each row's route and requirements.
Bayreuth and RPTU Kaiserslautern require basic German (A1, or an A1 course or A2 certificate) within the first year of study, though not to apply.

Focused programme refresh: 20 existing rows corresponding to the 26 institutions discussed were reconciled on 2026-11-10. The other 41 rows retain prior research but carry Window unverified rather than stale current-status claims.

Six discussed institutions have no qualifying row under the audited gates: HU Berlin, HM Munich UAS, HafenCity University, Goethe Frankfurt, Hohenheim and University Duisburg-Essen. Their findings and unresolved leads are recorded in the 2026-11-10 research ledger; a flagship-only exclusion is not an exhaustive catalogue audit.

Tanima’s profile records the inspected academic/language documents and user-reported Ilmenau offer separately. Grades and language scores do not replace official subject-credit equivalence or an inspected offer letter.

TU Ilmenau remains a user-reported offer baseline in the profile, not a ranked dataset row: EduRank 2026 overall 1,148 exceeds the nationwide 1,000 ceiling and Ilmenau is not in the existing 23-city exception list. No rank rule was changed.
